newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies tumble into close.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies tumble into close.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures alike tumbled late on sell stops to close with sharp losses, traders said.
Hog futures closed 1.225 to 0.050 cent per lb lower with June off 0.625 at 84.050 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.650 to 0.725 lower with July off 1.475 at 86.950 cents.

Profit taking and long liquidation prompted by ideas cash markets may have topped weighed on hog futures all day and touched off sell stops late. Farmers will be finishing the bulk of spring planting soon and hog marketings should pick up then, traders said.

"We are coming into a seasonal down in the next couple of weeks - we're working through our tighest (hog) numbers right now and we will have more hogs," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for for Frontier Risk Management.
Traders also cited reports that loin and butt prices are near a top and will soon retreat along with other pork cuts.

Rand Financials notably sold June through August during the day. E.D.&F. Man sold August on the late break. Cargill Investor Services and Refco spread long July/short June, thought to be the "Goldman roll", pit sources said.

In hog options commission houses sold June 81 and 83 puts and July 90 calls while buying December 74 calls. Futures traders were taking bearish options positions buy buying August 76 puts and selling June 86 calls on a two-for-one basis, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures also traded mixed on uncertainty over the weekly CME out-of-town storage report early, but retreated late as more traders looked for an in-movement last week. Some fund liquidation also developed on the break and this pushed prices down into sell stops late. July fell to a one week low on the setback, traders said.

Estimates on the report ranged from an in-movement of 1.0 million lbs to an out-movement of 300,000 lbs and speculation grew late that a fairly large in-movement would be reported. Weakness in cash bellies also encouraged bearish ideas.
After the close, the CME reported a net in-movement last week of 836,000 lbs versus an out-movement of 952,000 lbs the previous week and a net in-movement of 659,000 lbs last year.
Rand Financials, R.J. O'Brien, Refco and LFG sold July early with R.J. O'Brien, Refco and RBH selling late, pit sources said.
